---
title: RL with AReaL
---

## Overview

The AReaL integration runs SearchAgent inside an AReaL rollout workflow. SearchAgent
owns the conversation, tool execution, limits, and trajectory metadata; AReaL owns
distributed rollout scheduling, optimization, checkpoints, and experiment tracking.

The repository provides separate GRPO and IGPO entry points:

- `searchagent.training.areal.train_dist`
- `searchagent.training.areal.train_igpo`

## Prerequisites

Install and validate [AReaL](https://github.com/inclusionAI/AReaL) using its official
instructions. SearchAgent intentionally has lightweight runtime dependencies, so
install SearchAgent into the working AReaL environment rather than installing the
full AReaL stack into a general SearchAgent environment.

The training cluster also needs:

- a reachable dataset;
- accessible search, embedding, and summarizer services;
- the model and tokenizer paths on every required node;
- Ray and AReaL name-resolution storage configured for the cluster.

## Configure the workflow

Start with `src/searchagent/config/training/train_areal.yaml`. Its `workflow.agent`
section is a training-specific `SearchAgentConfig`:

```yaml
workflow:
  answer_pattern: '\\boxed\{(?P<answer>[^}]*)\}'
  agent:
    llm_client:
      type: openai
      model: ${actor.path}
    parser:
      type: upstream
    sources: []
    tools: []
    max_turn: 50
    max_tokens: 40960
    raise_repeat_tool_call: false
```

During rollout, `ARealClient` routes generation through AReaL instead of a standalone
OpenAI server. `SearchAgentTraining` additionally detects multiple parallel tool calls
and, when enabled, repeated calls with identical arguments.

Keep `eval_workflow` separate when evaluation should use different limits, sources, or
sampling behavior.

## Run training

Edit service and dataset paths in the config or override them at launch:

```bash
bash scripts/areal/train_dist_areal.sh \
  actor.path=/models/Qwen3-8B \
  train_dataset.path=/data/train.jsonl \
  cluster.n_nodes=2
```

The scripts contain cluster-specific defaults and are templates, not portable
one-command setups. Review GPU topology, backends, paths, concurrency, and batch size
before launch.

## Errors and reward assignment

Inference normally retries transient failures and records a failed sample after the
task policy is exhausted. Training must also assign a deterministic outcome to failed
or malformed rollouts so group statistics remain valid.

SearchAgent reward metadata separates:

- answer quality (`outcome_score`) in f1 score;
- context-length penalty (`overlong_penalty`);
- truncation penalty;
- tool-call count and repeated-query penalties.

Fatal error, and/or any errors that would surface, including exhausted retries, are to interrupt the rollout process and cause RL engine to dump the task.

## IGPO with AReaL

IGPO is implemented as an AReaL-specific trainer and workflow. The entry point is
`searchagent.training.areal.train_igpo`, which loads the IGPO trainer, carries the
ground-truth answer through `ARealIGPOSearchAgentWorkflow`, and computes the actor-side
IGPO objective with the FSDP actor implementation.

Use the dedicated config and launcher:

```bash
bash scripts/areal/train_dist_areal_igpo.sh \
  actor.path=/models/Qwen3-8B \
  train_dataset.path=/data/train.jsonl \
  cluster.n_nodes=2
```

IGPO needs reference answers in the training samples. In addition to the scalar
outcome and format signals described below, the actor can use answer log-probabilities
to form the IGPO advantage. Monitor answer-scoring throughput and the resulting IGPO
advantage statistics separately from ordinary GRPO rewards.

## Monitoring

At minimum, track:

- rollout completion and failure/error rate by exception type;
- reward mean, variance, and group acceptance rate;
- outcome, format, overlength, truncation, and search reward components;
- tool calls, repeated queries, and context tokens per trajectory;
- policy KL, clipping fraction, entropy, loss, and gradient norm.
